mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during triggered months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 6-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate revenue growth and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the industrial production index above 0.5% signals improving manufacturing activity and higher earnings potential, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points and a decline in average hourly earnings (GDPC1) over 3 months signals deteriorating labor cost dynamics, which reduces profit margins and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp AND GDPC1 falls over 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% combined with a consumer price index increase above 3% over 6 months signals a restrictive monetary regime, which increases discount rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% AND CPIAUCSL rises > 3% over 6 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 12-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) above 10% signals weakening residential investment and lower construction-related earnings, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points combined with a decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over 2 months signals accelerating labor market weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp AND PAYEMS falls over 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).
